subject: tech
title: Data and Pictures
about: Data is the information a computer keeps: numbers, words, pictures and sounds (K2-DA-02). The cards zoom into a picture to find its tiny dots, show the same counts as a tally chart and as a picture graph (K2-DA-03), predict from a graph (K2-DA-04), and use numbers and symbols to stand for things, like 1 for on and A for 1 (K2-AP-02, K2-NI-01). Read it together and point at the graph while he counts.
tip: Ask everyone at dinner their favorite fruit, make tally marks on paper, then draw the same answers as a picture graph and show him they match.

cards.q: Numbers, words, pictures and sounds a computer keeps all have one name. What is it?
cards.note: Data is information a computer keeps. Your photos and your game scores are data.

cards.q: You take a photo on the tablet and it saves it. What is the photo now?
cards.note: Pictures, songs and words all become data inside a computer.

cards.q: You zoom way in on a picture. What do you see?
cards.note: A picture is made of tiny dots called pixels. Zoom in and they look like little squares.

cards.q: The tiny dots that make up a picture have a name. What is it?
cards.note: Pixel is short for picture element. Millions of them make one photo.

cards.q: Which one is data a tablet can keep?
cards.note: Sounds are data too. The tablet keeps a song as a long list of numbers.

cards.q: You want to know the class's favorite pet. How do you collect the data?
cards.note: Collecting data means asking or counting. Each answer is one piece of data.

cards.q: Each tally mark is one kid who likes dogs. How many kids like dogs?
cards.note: Tally marks count in bundles of five: four lines and one across. Five and two more is seven.

cards.q: Each tally mark is one kid who likes cats. How many kids like cats?
cards.note: Four lines, no bundle yet. One more would make five and close the bundle.

cards.q: Look at the picture graph. How many kids like cats?
cards.sayQ: Look at the picture graph. Each picture is one kid. How many kids like cats?
cards.note: Count the cat row. A picture graph shows data with one picture for each one.

cards.q: 7 kids like dogs. You can show it with tally marks or with 7 dog pictures. What is the same?
cards.note: Same data, two ways to show it. A tally chart and a picture graph tell the same story.

cards.q: Look at the graph of snack picks. Which snack should we buy more of?
cards.sayQ: Look at the picture graph of snack picks. Each picture is one kid. Which snack should we buy more of?
cards.note: The longest row shows what most kids want. Using data to guess well is called a prediction.

cards.q: Look at the snack graph. Which snack will the fewest kids take?
cards.sayQ: Look at the picture graph of snack picks. Each picture is one kid. Which snack will the fewest kids take?
cards.note: The shortest row is the one fewest kids picked. You can predict it will be left over.

cards.q: Inside a computer, 1 can mean on and 0 can mean off. The light is on. Which number?
cards.note: Computers use just 1 and 0 to stand for things: on and off, yes and no.

cards.q: Under a photo, a little heart picture means something. What does it mean?
cards.note: A symbol is a little picture that stands for an idea. Heart means like.

cards.q: In a code, A is 1, B is 2, C is 3. What number is C?
cards.note: Numbers can stand for letters. Computers keep words as numbers like this.

cards.q: In the code A is 1, B is 2, C is 3, what letter is 2?
cards.note: Read the code backwards: 2 stands for B. You could send a secret number message!

cards.q: A big picture is sent in little pieces, then put back together. What is it like?
cards.note: Computers send big things in small pieces and put them back together, like a jigsaw puzzle.

cards.q: A long message is cut into small pieces to send. What happens to the pieces at the other end?
cards.note: Each piece has a number so they go back in the right order.
